fwci: Typical work: for works published 2021–2022, the median FWCI is 0.07–0.14. In every year, half of the works received at most 14% of the citations expected for similar works worldwide (FWCI 1 = world average).
Above the world average: 0% of the works per year have an FWCI above 1.
Not cited: on average 33% of these works have FWCI 0, meaning no citations within their four-year window. That is why many boxes start at 0.

Mean versus median: the mean is above the median in 2 of 2 years, because a few highly cited works pull the average up. The widest gap is 2022: mean 0.25, median 0.14, top work 0.8. The median is the better guide to a typical work.
Still counting: works from 2023 and 2025 have not completed their four-year citation window, so their values will rise. Do not compare them with older years yet.
Small base: the values for 2021–2023 and 2025 are based on only 10–29 works (lighter box or hollow point), so read them with care.
Few works: 2020, 2024 and 2026 have fewer than 10 works (2020: 5, 2024: 6, 2026: 5), too few for a box. Each of those works is drawn as a dot.
